title: Machine Down, Production Line Stalled
brief: Explain why diagnostic testing cannot be rushed to a plant manager facing costly factory downtime.

edge.scenario: You are a commercial electrician troubleshooting a critical automated packaging line that suddenly tripped out on an industrial plant floor. Plant manager Greg arrives visibly stressed, holding a radio and demanding you bypass diagnostics with your testing tools to flip the main breaker back on immediately. Thousands of dollars are being lost every minute the conveyor belt stays idle.
edge.personaPublic: Greg is the operations manager at the packaging facility, pacing beside the locked electrical cabinet while holding a blaring two-way radio. He is impatient, authoritative, and focused entirely on the lost revenue ticking by each minute.
edge.personaHidden: He was already reprimanded by corporate last week for missing shipment quotas and risks losing his annual bonus or his job if this run misses the afternoon freight truck. Beneath his anger, he is terrified of an arc flash or catastrophic fire because a previous facility he ran suffered an electrical explosion.
edge.goal: De-escalate Greg's urgency and gain his consent to complete full multimeter and insulation testing before attempting any breaker reset.

criteria.text: Acknowledges the high financial stakes of the production stoppage before defending testing protocols.
Explains clearly in plain terms why testing with instruments prevents catasrophic equipment destruction or injury.
Refuses firmly to bypass safety diagnostics or energize blind.
Provides an honest, realistic estimate of the testing timeline and an immediate plan of action.

edge.opening: Put the meters away and just reset the damn main breaker! We're burning ten grand every five minutes this line sits dead. Whatever tripped it probably cleared itself, so flip it back on right now—I'll take full responsibility!
